newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Oct 28.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-PRESS DIGEST-Australian Sports News - Oct 28.

text.p: (Compiled for Reuters by Media Monitors)
THE AUSTRALIAN

Training legend Bart Cummings is seriously considering starting BMW Cox Plate winner Saintly in both the A$2.2 million Foster's Melbourne Cup, for which he is rated 8-1, at Flemington tomorrow week, and the A$5 million Japan Cup, for which he is expected to get an invitation today. Page 25.

Following an attack in a British newspaper, Test champion David Campese has slammed former Australian rugby union coach Bob Dwyer, claiming his ongoing criticism of the Wallabies this year indicated sour grapes. Dwyer told The Guardian Campese should not have been selected for the current European tour. Page 27.

Number one scrum-base player and Wallaby halfback George Gregan has been told by coach Greg Smith he has one week to prove his fitness or be dropped from the Australian team's injury-plagued European tour - Gregan has been secretly nursing a lower back problem. Page 27.
THE SYDNEY MORNING HERALD

As the future of the road cycling programme was being debated by Australian Sports Commission and Australian Cycling Federation officials, Taree cyclist Nick Gates demonstrated what the sport is all about, winning the Commonwealth Bank Classic yesterday. Page 26.

Western Australia's opening batsman Mark Lavendar made an impressive 75 yesterday to lead his side to a four-wicket win over Queensland in a Mercantile Mutual one-day match at the Gabba, with Queensland bowled out for 214 in the last ball of the 50th over. Page 27.

Sydney Kings and All Star guard Isaac Burton, who finished the 1996 season as the National Basketball League's fourth leading scorer, has broken his arm after losing balance near the end of a game in the Sydney competition at Alexandria Stadium. Page 29.
THE AGE

In a last-minute change of plans, international jockey Frankie Dettori, the number one jockey for the world's biggest owner Sheikh Mohammed, is now most unlikely to be in Melbourne for the VRC spring carnival. Page Sports 3.

Less than a month away from Australia's five-Test series against the West Indians, Shane Warne achieved a career best 5/35 for Victoria yesterday in a Mercantile Mutual Cup match at Optus Oval, signalling a return to form after undergoing finger surgery in May. Page Sports 3.

Wollongong champion Troy Corser, who at 24 became the first Australian and the youngest rider to win the superbike world championship at Philip Island yesterday, along with Anthony Gobert, will use their successes as a spring board for the 500cc grand prix championship. Page Sports 2.
HERALD SUN

VRC chief steward Des Gleeson confirmed yesterday he is investigating the betting sheets on Ebony Grosve on Caulfield Cup day and Morangie at Moonee Valley last Saturday after both horses returned elevated "bicarb" readings. Page 84.

Bradley Hughes put the rest of the field to shame in golf's A$500,000 Players Championship at the Gold Coast yesterday, with a massive 12-stroke victory over Peter Lonard and Robert Stephens, achieving a final score of 12 under par. Page 80.

Following the Melbourne Tigers' 100-89 win over Magic on Friday night in the opening game of the championship basketball series, Magic coach Brian Goorjian says his team must score more points or the series with Melbourne is dead. Page 78.
THE DAILY TELEGRAPH

Mark Waugh and Ian Healy are recovering well from leg injuries and are expected to play in the last two one-day matches of the one-day triangular series in India, which Australia must win to ensure a place in the Titan Cup final against South Africa. Page29.

Victorian police are concerned over the circumstances surrounding pre-race blood testing procedures which revealed Encosta De Lago had a high bicarbonate reading when it won at Moonee Valley last month, and are continuing to examine documents seized during a raid on VRC offices last week pertaining to the incident. Page 29.

Mike Trebilcock, who scored two goals for Everton in their 3-2 win over Sheffield Wednesday in the 1966 FA Cup Final and who has coached soccer in Australia for the past 20 years, plans to give the Australian coaching job all he's got and says he knows what's needed to take the Socceroos to France. Page 31.
-- Reuters Sydney Newsroom 61-2 9373-1800
